newsitem.title: USA: Claridge Hotel says regrets bankruptcy filing.
newsitem.headline: Claridge Hotel says regrets bankruptcy filing.

text.p: The Claridge Hotel & Casino Corp said on Wednesday it "regrets" that three noteholders have decided to file a petition forcing the company into bankruptcy.
Under bankruptcy rules, any three noteholders with $10,000 worth of its notes in the aggregate may file such a petition.
The company said in a statement that it "regrets" that action was taken. It said it would respond to the petition at the "appropriate time."
The move comes less than a week after a committee of noteholders sued Claridge in an attempt to garner full redemption value of outstanding first mortgage notes.
Claridge had indicated it would not make a scheduled February interest payment on the notes, sending the company into default.

The petition puts Claridge in a gap period, a lawyer for the noteholders, David Pikus, said earlier on Wednesday. In that time, Claridge can operate but can also have the advantage of an automatic stay, which could suspend any litigation or claims against the company.

Although Claridge did not make its $5 million interest payment due on February 3, Claridge said it has adequate cash to pay all of its normal on-going expenses, including payroll, trade payables and payouts to gamblers.

"The reason we chose not to pay the interest is to ensure that we continue to have adequate funds available, to pay all other obligations," President and Chief Executive Robert Renneisen said in a statement.
"We have no concerns about being able to meet all other current liabilities and requirements as they come due."
